nodes.label: Benedito (the man without a name)
nodes.rationale: Working name only; never named in the book. Born c. 1846, crioulo on a Recôncavo sugar estate; freed by the war; wins the lottery; buys farms at Jacadigo.

nodes.label: Carmen (the woman from Spain)
nodes.rationale: Working name only; never named. Born c. 1858 near Vigo, Galicia; trafficked via Buenos Aires to Corumbá; bought by Benedito and married.

nodes.label: Luzia
nodes.rationale: Nagô healer, midwife and singer; Benedito's mother; sold south c. 1858; buys her freedom c. 1866; dies c. 1873 in Cachoeira.

nodes.label: Inácio (Benedito's father)
nodes.rationale: Enslaved boiling-house worker; dies of cholera 1855.

nodes.label: Coronel Joaquim Araújo de Menezes
nodes.rationale: Senhor de engenho in the Recôncavo; 'good master' in debt; sells Luzia; offers enslaved men to the army.

nodes.label: Liberdade (farm)
nodes.rationale: Benedito's farm at Jacadigo; owns no one.

nodes.label: Zuavos baianos
nodes.rationale: All-Black companies of Bahian volunteers, 1865; later merged into line battalions.

nodes.label: Dom Obá II (Cândido da Fonseca Galvão)
Luck and the gambling inheritance
nodes.rationale: Luck as a worldview passed down: orixás → luck → cards → grandma's lottery.
